cells.tense: The adjustments are being made right now, and the one making them is here.
cells.act: keep the ritual and give it room to change
cells.ask: Keep the weekly thing you do the same way each time — and this week change a single detail: the order, the hour, who's there. Keep the rest exactly as it is.
cells.core:
You read a room fast — what to add, what to take out — and you do it while the room is still moving. That's the skill. Where you're centered it shows up as small adjustments nobody announces: you say less here, more there, and the thing keeps going without anyone having to name what you did. You catch what counts before you've found the words, and you act on it.

There's something you keep doing the same way. Keep doing it, and change one detail — the order, the timing, who's standing there. Just the one. You'll see what the ritual was carrying and what was only habit, and the habit part is yours to move. Nothing breaks. The people who do it with you will barely notice, which is how you'll know it still works.
cells.sheetLine: What you notice first usually turns out to be right.
cells.verb: sensing what to add and what to take out, and keeping the flow
cells.place: a place where you know what counts before you've found the words

cells.tense: The smoothing runs first, settling the room before anyone says what they mean.
cells.act: move toward the thing you want, one step, today
cells.ask: Think of something you want that would surprise someone close to you. Take one small step toward it today, before the room settles into its usual shape.
cells.core:
You feel a room move and you're already leveling it — taking the edge off before it's spoken, agreeing before anyone's disagreed. The skill is real. Right now it runs first, and the leveling has stopped being adjustment and started being the thing you do instead of the moment. What can't be said gets quietly filed as not worth saying, and the filing is yours.

Wanting is allowed to show. Think of something you want that would surprise someone close to you — not a big announcement, one small move toward it today, before the room settles into its usual shape. Feel where the pull is and follow it a step. The people who matter can stand to see you want something. You'll find out who can, which is information you don't have yet.
cells.sheetLine: You smooth the room before anyone has spoken.

cells.tense: The moment passed while attention was still scattered across the one before it.
cells.act: let yourself be reached by what they are carrying
cells.ask: Next time someone tells you something hard, stay where you are. Don't fix it, don't match it. Let what they're carrying land on you before you answer.
cells.core:
Things come at you and each one takes a piece — a message, a face, a mood — and by the time you look, you're not sure which of them you were actually in. It isn't that you don't care. It's that the middle of you is hard to find from here, and the adjustments go out to every direction at once. You've been standing at the last door while this one opened.

Someone near you is carrying something. Next time they say it, stay present — don't fix it, don't match it, don't hand it back. Let it land on you where you are, and notice what it feels like when it does. Being reached is not the same as being pulled apart. You can keep your own side while it happens. That's what comes back first — not calm, just contact.
cells.sheetLine: You're still at the last door while this one opens.
cells.verb: sensing what to add and what to take out, and keeping the flow
cells.place: a place where you know what counts before you've found the words

cells.tense: The balance is being kept, and the one keeping it hasn't marked it as theirs.
cells.act: teach it the way it was taught to you, with one change
cells.ask: Pass on a skill someone once showed you. Show it the way it came to you, and add one adjustment of your own. That's the whole ask.
cells.core:
You balance without noticing you're doing it — the read on the room, the small moves, the timing. It runs, and it runs well, and your account of yourself doesn't include it. You'd say the situation called for it, or the other person needed it, or it was nothing. The adjustments are yours. You've been filing them under circumstance.

Someone taught you something you now do well — a way of handling a conversation, a way of holding a group. Pass it on the way it came to you, and add one adjustment you'd make. That's the whole ask. Saying it out loud — even to a single person — is where you find out the knowledge has an author, and the author is you. You'll hear your own voice in it, which is what you've been not hearing.
cells.sheetLine: The balance you keep is yours, filed under circumstance.

cells.place: a place where you know what counts before you've found the words
